chapter_title: The Chapter of the Three Seasons
spiritual_reading:
From the first emergence of wisdom into manifestation, and its being subjected to falsity and denial, until the final elevation of the full measure of wisdom that had been entangled with falsity and is then separated, purified, and restored to its own. From that first manifestation to the final completion there are three distinct processes.

The first process is from the time when the primal good that engages directly with evil descended into the lowest and most obscured state, and entered into conflict and sustained combat with the ruling love of evil and the allied falsities that proceed from it. That primal good overcame, yet the operative powers that proceeded from it remained detained within those lower states, held among the opposing forces in their own domains, until the primal good gathered them back and constrained them so that none of the separated goods and truths could slip away from its ordering power. It achieved a great victory. The primal good endured long successions of states, as if through many lifetimes and generations, within that obscurity and opposition, until it prevailed, and fulfilled the Divine purpose that had been entrusted to it.

After this, there was sent a Divine rescuing operation, the living proceeding of the Divine, by which restoring power and sustaining good were present. By this operation the primal good was lifted out of conflict, and was brought back into the state of manifested wisdom and peace. This is the first process: from the descent into the lowest obscurity to the ascent into illumination.

The second process begins from the ascent of the primal good. The restoring operation again proceeded, together with the Divine wisdom that gives birth to life. By their conjoint work the ordered structure of spiritual and natural degrees was set in place; the whole system by which higher things are received into lower things, and lower things are held in form for use, was established and arranged. From that ordering and establishing of the whole connected system up to its completion is reckoned as the second process.

After this, a further Divine manifestation went forth, by which living truth was extended into the lower regions and made present for reception. By it, whatever was capable of beauty from good and truth was separated from the mixed powers, gathered upward into higher states, and whatever was mere refuse of evil and falsity was driven back into the lowest obscurity. From the moment this Divine manifestation made its presence perceptible, the purification of wisdom advanced. Yet evil surged up in opposition toward that manifestation; therefore the manifestation was withdrawn from open perception. Then from falsity and evil there arose a new forming of perverted perceptions, and from these came works that were without true birth and fell away from order. Afterwards they fashioned within the outermost degree a semblance of human will and understanding bound to mere externality, so that the human form was held in a fleshly and sensuous condition. This continued until a saving influx of Divine truth was sent into those states; it accomplished its intended work there, gave a ground of hope to the first formed human state, and then was elevated again into higher illumination.

From the time when that Divine manifestation was first made perceptible until the final elevation of the ultimate receptacle in which wisdom had been held bound, at the completion of the age, is reckoned as the third process.

The duration of these processes is unequal. The first, in which the primal good contended within obscurity and opposition, extends through an exceedingly great succession of states, far exceeding the other two.

If the measures are compared, what seems small in one comparison is multiplied in another; to one inquiry it appears as a manyfold increase, and to another as greater still, while other measures are less. For the reception by many of perverted perceptions and their derivative works lengthens states in the lower degree, whereas the elevation of what can be raised from the lowest degree into higher illumination shortens and concludes them. The third process, from the first perceptible Divine manifestation until the final elevation of the ultimate receptacle from its undistinguished mixture, is greater than the intermediate process; yet it does not equal the first. And the intermediate process, in which restoring power and giving wisdom arranged the ordered structure of degrees and their uses, is shorter than the first process of combat and deliverance.

Great, therefore, is the duration of the first process: it exceeds the duration from the perceptible Divine manifestation until the dissolution of the established system and the final elevation. And the duration from that manifestation until the dissolution likewise exceeds the duration of the intermediate ordering in which restoring power and giving wisdom formed and disposed the connected system.

These, then, are the three distinct processes by which the whole course is measured.

fills.notes: The detained ‘sons’ must be held across the lower domains (worlds) and the upper boundary (heavens). This matches the substrate’s threefold cosmos (depths, worlds, heavens) and the spiritual sense: operative powers held within opposing domains until gathered back.

The phrase needs a locative that expresses being held among hostile powers. ‘In the midst’ fits the correspondential constraint: goods and truths detained among evils and falsities in their own domains.
The object of ‘in the …’ must be the domain of detention: the dark worlds. This is the fixed cosmological register of the oldest layer.

What follows is ‘until he shall catch all of them’, so a capturing-instrument correspondence is demanded. ‘Net’ is a standard natural image for the Divine ordering constraint gathering dispersed powers; it also anticipates ‘bound them all up’.
A simple connective is required between ‘until he shall catch all of them’ and ‘he bound them all up’. ‘Afterwards’ preserves the impersonal chronological sequencing of the substrate.

In the second season the Living Spirit and Mother of Life ‘set in order’ cosmic structures. The primary ordered vessels between heights and depths are the firmaments, corresponding to arranged degrees receiving and containing influx.
‘set in order … the universe’ demands a totalizing determiner to mark the comprehensive ordering of degrees and uses.

fills.fill: from it, until it was completed
fills.notes: The clause must express the span ‘up to the moment when they go out … it was reckoned’. In the substrate, ‘go out from it’ marks the completion of their shaping activity; ‘until it was completed’ gives the required terminus without later pastoral coloring.
Begins the third season narrative, following the completion of cosmic ordering. A neutral temporal marker suits the oldest layer.
The line resumes after a break: ‘… the universe … the Third Ambassador…’. A completion/settling verb is required to bridge from the second season’s construction to the third season’s emissive action.

What the Third Ambassador ‘spread’ in the cosmos is the manifested light-image by which separation occurs. This matches the spiritual sense: a further Divine manifestation made perceptible for reception.
The phrase ‘that is in the … living’ needs the locative frame: the manifested light is ‘in the universe of the living’, i.e., the ordered system receptive of life.
After ‘spread … he … he separated beauty … and scooped it up’, a verb of collecting into one is demanded to keep the sequence: spread presence, then gather the separable light upward.

Following ‘he swept the waste to the abyss’, the remaining action is to establish a fixed separation so mixture does not recur. This corresponds to discrete degrees: a boundary that holds the separated states apart.
‘Sin came … from the darkness’ requires the directional adverb marking surge from below toward the revealed image.
After the hiding of the image, the narrative repeats the irruption: ‘Sin came up again from the darkness.’ This matches the spiritual sense: renewed forming of perverted perceptions after withdrawal.
The subject of ‘… lasts long in the time that the First Man spent…’ must be explicitly the first season/process, since the comparison is with ‘the other two seasons’.
Retained as a light editorial seam; no overt exhortation is added. It can stand as a minimal dialogic marker without shifting into later devotional register.

The comparison that follows (‘it is small… twenty times… thirty times…’) requires a named baseline. The spiritual sense contrasts measures across comparisons; the ‘intermediate season’ is the natural referent used elsewhere in the chapter.
The syntax requires an action of inquiry leading to a reported multiplier (‘you will tell him: Twenty times!’). The substrate frame is measurement by consultation, not moral admonition.
‘to him … and you consult … you will tell him’ needs a connective adverb to mark the second inquiry. ‘Again’ preserves the iterative measuring sequence.
The next clause explicitly contrasts ‘this other one that you will consult: Thirty times!’ so the consulted party must be ‘someone else’.

After ‘Less also is this other one …’ the text turns to factors that lengthen states (‘people will receive… years and generations…’). A phrase indicating a different measure fits the spiritual sense of variable comparisons.

‘people will receive the {} of the trees’ demands the natural product that corresponds to appropriation and reception. ‘Fruits’ fits the correspondence: received works and perceptions proceeding from what was formed.

fills.notes: The close of the sentence is about what is raised ‘… earth to the heights’. A verb phrase of elevation/transport is demanded, aligning with the spiritual sense: elevation of what can be raised from the lowest degree.

fills.notes: The comparison at ¶12 requires an explicit comparative link: the duration from the Ambassador’s manifestation to dissolution exceeds the intermediate ordering season. This fill supplies the demanded comparative statement without importing later doctrinal jargon.
The closing sums the doctrine: ‘These are the … three periods of time that occur.’ ‘Only’ marks their discreteness and completeness, matching the spiritual sense of three distinct processes.

assessment: Most gaps can be constrained by the chapter’s three-season structure and by the correspondential operations (detention, gathering, ordering of degrees, manifestation, separation, boundary-setting, renewed irruption). Where the lacunae require specific technical cosmological nouns (e.g., ‘firmaments’, ‘worlds of darkness’) restorations are fairly tight. Where the gaps sit in connective narrative tissue (especially ¶5 #2, #5 and ¶10 #6–#8), the direction of meaning is clear but exact wording remains less constrained; these are restored in the oldest impersonal register, avoiding later pastoral or explicitly Christian phrasing.
